cards.gateNote: Classical MHD/error-field study. No quantum hardware, and it does not by itself close a tearing-avoidance RL loop.
Numerics on 1D chains. Prethermal lifetime vs a control horizon is still the kill test, and it is not passed here.
Proposal / model. No public logical qubit.
Sheath / wall code, not a driven-Coulomb-barrier fusion-rate engine. Does not move Layer 2 off HOLD.
Thesis, not a plant Q. No Floquet nuclear tunneling.
Linear MHD surrogate. Fail if a quantum path is slower or less accurate on the same model.
Holography as a reactor or processor subsystem is on the denylist (E-HOL CUT). One paper cannot un-cut it.
Processor analog. G5: does not treat a QPU demo as a tokamak result.

gates.note: Closed threshold proof vs stochastic baseline; platform-honest (codes, not a tokamak).

cards.math: Coherent Z-rotation noise on qLDPC / surface code; ML Pauli recovery. Breaks if noise is generic non-Pauli coherent.
cards.disputer: Proof is Z-type coherent rotations, not a non-Abelian decoder.

plain.core: Real devices make coherent over-rotations, not just random bit flips. This paper proves a positive threshold still exists for that noise on surface-code-like codes.
plain.why: DBE braids will be miscalibrated. A coherent-error theorem is more honest than a stochastic slogan.
plain.limit: Does not cover generic non-Pauli coherent noise or non-Abelian anyon decoding.

gates.note: G3: compilation study, not vs a named MHD baseline, so no C raise.

cards.math: Compile molecular / condensed-phase propagators onto Fibonacci/Ising braids. Breaks if leakage or compilation depth exceeds hardware.
cards.claimDelta: E-S3 C3 → C3; queued suggested pillar topo-dynamics
cards.disputer: A bounded quantum advantage on toy dynamics is not in-loop plasma control (latency kill test).

plain.core: Topological hardware can compile quantum dynamics, not only static molecular energies.
plain.why: This is a Bus B job: offline simulation on S3/Fibonacci, never a tokamak in-loop braid.
plain.limit: Does not attach to a plant API and must not skip the latency bound.

gates.note: Journal hardware on trapped ions. Caps C at 3 because it is not a tokamak (G5).

cards.math: S3 quantum double; C2 fluxes; braid + fusion + X/Z measurements. Unitarity of fusion space preserved.
cards.claimDelta: E-S3 C3 stays (already set by this paper at freeze)
cards.disputer: Linear-depth with post-selection at 54 qubits; constant-depth adaptive is the scalable claim, not this shot.

plain.core: On 54 trapped-ion qubits, S3 anyons were prepared and braided+fused into a universal qutrit gate set, including a magic state.
plain.why: This is the actual braid primitive. Majorana is no longer the only topological path.
plain.limit: Processor analog, not a reactor part. C cannot exceed 3 by G5.

gates.note: Journal nuclear theory vs thermal rate. Conservative ledger move (required E up).

cards.math: Floquet/Volkov DT tunneling at 1 keV. Breaks if hole-burning + SRS/SBS are omitted from the rate.
cards.claimDelta: S-L2 C1 as gain path stays; required E bound recorded
cards.disputer: PRC 110 finds even harsher irradiance. KH vs FV disagreement keeps the gain-path at C1.
cards.ledger: E ~ 1e15–1e16 V/m; ħω ≲ 1 keV; DT at 1 keV

plain.core: Laser-assisted DT tunneling is real theory, but the field needed is next-gen XFEL, not a tokamak antenna.
plain.why: Sets the Layer-2 fail threshold the daily run is required to hunt.
plain.limit: No fusion-gain experiment. Does not write a plant Q.

gates.note: Nature hardware on DIII-D. Relevant class of machine (C4).

cards.math: RL policy on shape/beta vs tearing onset. Baseline is the lab controller.
cards.claimDelta: E-RL C4 stays; T3 confirmed on DIII-D
cards.disputer: Tearing avoidance ≠ Q_eng. Quantum in this loop still fails the latency kill test.

plain.core: A deep-RL agent on DIII-D saw tearing coming and moved the plasma out of the way using the real coils.
plain.why: The only DBE piece that already talks to a fusion plant.
plain.limit: Classical controller. Do not smuggle a quantum processor into the Alfvén time.

cards.disputer: Andreev / YSR mimics still explain many zero-bias peaks.
